column3: NKJV has “high priests” (plural), following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the singular “high priesthood.”
Close to the Greek; “forgiveness” is rendered “remission.”
NKJV has “What shall we do then?,” following the Textus Receptus wording; the critical text uses a different form of the verb with the same sense.
Close to the Greek; “extort” is rendered “intimidate.”
NKJV has “He will thoroughly clean out … and gather,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the infinitives “to clean out … and to gather.”
NKJV includes “Philip,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “his brother's wife.”
NKJV spells the name “Janna”; the critical text has “Jannai.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV spells the name “Mattathiah.”
NKJV reads “Semei, … Joseph, … Judah,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Semein, … Josech, … Joda.”
NKJV spells the name “Joannas”; the critical text has “Joanan.”

NKJV reads “Jose,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Joshua.”
